Subject: Tenant provisioning playlist + initial admin check-in

Hi Alice —

Great to be kicking this off. Attached is a short ‘provisioning playlist’ we use to get a tenant live: project naming, admin seed, API key seeding, and invite windows. For our first pass I suggest we: 

- Create one project called kitelab-prod and a sandbox project called kitelab-dev.
- Provide 2 admin users from your side who can approve API key requests and manage roles.
- Redwood seeds a scoped admin API key (limited lifetime) to get initial configs in place; you can rotate after we hand over.
- Schedule a 30-min technical handoff this week to confirm project IDs and invite emails.

Action items for KiteLab: please reply with the two admin email addresses you want as initial owners and confirm whether you need dedicated capacity or will start on hosted.

Attachments: tenant-access-playlist.xlsx (checklist), SOW-draft.pdf (for your procurement team)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Thanks Alice — helpful questions. Short answers up front, details below: 

1) Scoped admin API key: Read/write on tenant admin endpoints only (project, roles, invites, key management). No access to billing. The seed key we supply is time-limited (30 days) and we provide a rotation command you can run immediately after we handoff. See attached api-key-seed-sample.txt for the curl pattern.

2) No IAM changes on KiteLab’s identity provider are required for the seed — all role assignments are represented inside Redwood’s tenant model. If you want SCIM or SAML provisioning, we can wire those after we confirm project/roles.

3) SSO: If you want SSO connected before invite rollouts to avoid account collisions, we can schedule a slightly longer window; otherwise it’s fine to invite users then attach SAML later. Most customers prefer to start invites after SSO is validated.

Suggested mutual action plan (high-level):
- Today: confirm admin emails and hosted vs dedicated decision (Alice)
- Tomorrow (10:00am PT): 30-minute technical handoff (Redwood CSM + Eng)
- Day +1: Redwood seeds admin key and creates kitelab-dev and kitelab-prod projects
- Day +2: KiteLab validates invites and rotates key

Monica will seed the key and post the one-time command into your Ops channel during the call. Dev will prepare the project templates.

If 10am PT tomorrow works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include the short agenda: 1) confirm project names, 2) review seed key lifecycle, 3) invite pattern and SSO note.

Laura
